title: A food foundation within the living guide

title: Protein targets: guidance, training and applicability
summary: Prepared for the user’s manual pull-request review. Added population-guidance and research context to the existing protein illustration, with related explanations in the priorities and longevity chapters. The 128-gram example and all training prescriptions remain unchanged.
scope: Reconstructed the proposed update after confirming the staging branch matched main. Compared current source hashes with the available guide files and considered all seven routes, chapter map, registry, history and verification code. Fresh research was limited to protein: inspected the federal guideline (printed page 2), scientific report (Chapter 6, pages 37–38), Nunes et al. full HTML methods/results/discussion/disclosures, and NIH ODS protein guidance. PDF pages were visually checked. Searches covered the current guideline, the 74-trial review, and DOI/guideline correction queries; this was not an exhaustive search. No appendices or individual trials were reappraised; unrelated sources were not freshly verified.
recommendationChange: The fictional 80-kilogram trainee still uses 1.6 g/kg/day = 128 g/day. The rationale now distinguishes population guidance, training research and practical synthesis. It does not create a universal minimum, general-health threshold, precise optimum or longevity dose. No new supplement, restrictive diet or disease-specific advice is introduced. Existing confidence labels and H01 remain unchanged.
verification: Local registry and transition validation and all 16 rehearsal tests passed. The full site build and generated-page checks use the existing branch/PR workflow because local GitHub DNS resolution failed. This record is a review candidate, not a claim of publication, production verification, independent clinical review or browser-based visual review.
next: User review and merge, followed by separate production verification. Expand dietary-pattern and food-adequacy coverage; investigate protein source and longer-term outcomes. Preserve the previous review entries as the history recorded at preparation time.

title: Full-text resistance-training check; prepared for manual merge

title: The founding edition
summary: Established the health-first charter, three connected chapters, an explicit worked week, a protein-arithmetic example, source-access records, and whole-guide dependency checks. This is a pilot foundation rather than completed coverage of nutrition and fitness.
scope: Read the complete initial guide and inspected 13 institutional or research sources through targeted lookup. Included current ACSM and WHO summaries, concurrent-training research, and methods guidance. This was not an exhaustive database search or a formal systematic review; source-specific access limitations are recorded. The mortality meta-analysis was inspected at abstract level only.
recommendationChange: Initial publication; there is no previous guide recommendation to reverse. The sample week and 128-gram protein calculation are practical illustrations, not validated optima or lifespan prescriptions. The fallback-adherence hypothesis remains unconfirmed and is not used to justify a superiority claim.
verification: The repository contains executable registry checks and 16 rehearsal tests. They test traceability and release mechanics, not medical accuracy. Build and test execution results are recorded by the Long Game checks workflow; no independent clinical review has occurred.
next: Inspect the full 2026 resistance-training position stand and its relevant constituent evidence; deepen dietary-pattern and food-adequacy coverage; examine progression and hypertrophy volume; develop evidence-supported adaptations for older adults and differing physical capabilities.
